title: Caching strategies
summary: Why and where to cache, read patterns (cache-aside, read-through) and write patterns (write-through, write-back), eviction policies, TTLs, and the stampede/thundering-herd problem.
note:
1. Cache = fast store for hot data (Redis, in-process, CDN)
2. Reads: cache-aside (app checks cache, fills on miss) · read-through (cache fetches)
3. Writes: write-through (write both, consistent, slower) · write-back (write cache, flush later, fast but risky)
4. Evict by LRU/LFU; set a TTL so stale data expires
5. Watch stampedes: many misses hit the DB at once → lock/early-refresh
✎ In my words: ______________________________________________

recall.q: How does cache-aside handle a miss?
recall.a: The app reads the cache, and on a miss loads from the DB, writes it back into the cache, then returns it.
Write-through keeps cache and DB consistent but is slower; write-back is fast but can lose data if the cache dies before flushing.

recall.q: What is a cache stampede and one fix?
recall.a: Many simultaneous misses hammer the DB when a hot key expires; fix with a lock/single-flight or early/background refresh.

shot.title: Cache patterns
shot.body:
| pattern | who talks to DB | notes |
|---|---|---|
| cache-aside | app | most common; lazy fill |
| read-through | cache | app only sees the cache |
| write-through | cache→DB sync | consistent, slower writes |
| write-back | cache→DB async | fast, risk on crash |

sections.title: Why and where to cache
sections.body: ✍️ A cache stores hot data in a faster/closer layer to cut latency and offload the database. Common layers: **in-process** (fast, per-node, not shared), **distributed** (Redis/Memcached, shared), and **CDN/edge** (static assets near users).

sections.title: Read patterns
Write patterns
sections.body: ✍️ **Write-through:** write cache and DB together — consistent, slower writes. **Write-back (write-behind):** write cache now, flush to DB asynchronously — fast but risks loss if the cache fails before flushing. A common safe default is write-through plus cache-aside reads, or simply invalidate the key on write.

sections.title: Eviction and TTL
sections.body:
✍️ Caches are bounded, so they evict. **LRU** drops least-recently-used; **LFU** drops least-frequently-used. A **TTL** auto-expires entries so stale data can't live forever.
- Short TTL = fresher but more misses; long TTL = cheaper but staler.

sections.title: The stampede problem
sections.body: ✍️ When a hot key expires, many concurrent requests miss at once and all hit the DB (thundering herd). Mitigate with a **single-flight lock** (one request refills, others wait), **early/background refresh** before expiry, or slightly randomized TTLs to avoid synchronized expiration.
